Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-30
Start time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Raman (Redwood SE), Luis Ortega (Redwood CSM), Tom Reynolds (Bluecrest CISO), Aisha Khan (Bluecrest Dir IT), Mark Li (Compliance Manager), Sara Voss (Procurement)

Summary (auto-gen - may be rough):
Quick posture review focused on SOC 2 and ISO 27001 artifacts, controls mapping for data residency and encryption, discuss SSO/RBAC and audit logs retention, surface next steps to exchange reports and schedule deeper technical session.

Topics: SOC 2 Type II report, ISO 27001 certificate, trust center access, controls mapping, RBAC / SSO (SAML), audit logs and retention, encryption/KMS (customer-managed keys), data residency, vendor management and subcontractors, penetration testing cadence.

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, um, appreciate you carving out the time. I'm Jordan Lee from Redwood, I'm the account executive on the Bluecrest engagement. With me is Priya Raman, our solutions engineer and Luis from customer success.
[00:15] Tom: Hey Jordan, thanks. Tom here. We'll jump in as needed — we've got Aisha and Mark as well.
[00:22] Aisha: Hi all.
[00:24] Mark: Morning — afternoon.
[00:26] Luis: Quick agenda — high level posture review, walk through the artifacts we can share, then go into controls mapping, and leave time for Q&A. Sound good?
[00:32] Tom: Yep. For context, Bluecrest has a SOC 2 program in process; we're doing vendor attestation and we run HIPAA adjacent workloads. We want to understand Redwood's controls surface, scope of SOC 2 and ISO, and how data residency and customer-managed keys work.
[00:45] Jordan: Totally. We'll start with the artifacts we often provide: SOC 2 Type II attestation, ISO 27001 cert, our trust center portal access for customers, controls mapping spreadsheet that maps Redwood controls to common frameworks, and the encryption/KMS docs.
[01:02] Priya: Quick note on terminology — sometimes the transcription might flip product names, but when we say "trust center" that's our secure portal where we share attestation reports and scoped diagrams.
[01:12] Mark: Great. First question: what's the scope of your SOC 2 Type II — infrastructure, platform, and any exclusions?
[01:22] Priya: Our SOC 2 Type II covers the hosted Redwood API and the dedicated control plane for hosted customers; it includes logical and physical access controls, change management, incident response, and encryption in transit and at rest for the services in scope. The report includes control narratives and test results for the 12-month period that they inspected. We also have ISO 27001 certification that overlaps but is broader in terms of ISMS processes.
[01:44] Tom: When you say "hosted API" — does that include any data persistence for logs or for prompt/response storage? We need to understand retention defaults and retention controls.
[01:55] Priya: By default, we retain request logs and non-consented debug traces for N days — that value varies by tenant type. For customers with stricter needs we offer dedicated retention policies and can disable request logging for privacy-sensitive flows. We'll share the retention table in the controls mapping doc.
[02:12] Aisha: And where is the data physically located? We're evaluating EU residency for some PHI-adjacent metadata.
[02:20] Jordan: Good question — we support region pinning for hosted customers in our EU region, and Dedicated/Private deployments allow you to keep everything in your VPC or on-prem which satisfies residency. For hosted, we can show the regions and the trust center has the list of regions and data centers we use.
[02:35] Mark: On encryption — is customer-managed KMS supported? We need to demonstrate to auditors that keys are under our control for certain workflows.
[02:43] Priya: Yes. For Private deployments and some Dedicated configurations we support customer-managed keys (CMKs) via AWS KMS and HSM integrations. For hosted API we currently offer Redwood-managed keys by default, and a bring-your-own-key option for enterprise tiers. Key rotation, usage logs, and separation of duties are documented in the KMS section of the trust center.
[03:03] Tom: Can you confirm whether encryption at rest covers model weights and any cached embeddings or are those considered ephemeral?
[03:12] Priya: Model artifacts that we persist in storage are encrypted at rest; KV cache is managed in memory for many runtime configurations but if it's persisted it's also encrypted. We can map exactly which artifacts are considered ephemeral vs persisted in the control spreadsheet.
[03:26] Luis: Also worth noting: our runtime supports configurable caching knobs — for strict compliance flows customers can opt out of assisted caching to avoid persisted derived artifacts.
[03:35] Aisha: SSO and RBAC — we use Okta and need SCIM and SAML support for automatic provisioning and group-based roles. How does Redwood handle roles and admin separation?
[03:45] Priya: We have RBAC with role templates (Admin, Developer, Auditor, Viewer) and SAML SSO for authentication. We support SCIM for provisioning in enterprise plans. Role assignments and audit trails for role changes are logged — logs are retained per the retention policy and exported to customer SIEMs on request.
[04:03] Mark: Do you have separation of duties for key management and access to audit logs?
[04:10] Priya: Yes — access to KMS configuration and key rotations is limited to a small set of platform ops roles, and audit log access can be delegated to separate teams. For Dedicated/Private deployments, customers can fully isolate key control.
[04:23] Tom: About audit logs — what events are captured and what's the retention? We need to show to our auditors that admin changes, API keys creation, and data-access events are logged.
[04:33] Priya: We capture admin actions, auth events, API key creates/deletes, configuration changes, and significant runtime events (e.g., model rollout changes). Default retention is 90 days for hosted; for enterprise/Dedicated we support longer retention and export to S3 or SIEM. We'll include the event list in the mapping doc.
[04:50] Jordan: I'll also flag that we can provide a vendor SOC 2 bridge letter for up-to-date context if a customer's audit window lines up.
[04:58] Sara: Procurement will need proof of subservice organizations — do you publish a list of subprocessors and do you have flow-down agreements?
[05:06] Priya: Yes, the trust center lists current subprocessors, change-notification commitments, and standard flow-down language. We maintain contractual obligations that align with SOC 2 and ISO requirements.
[05:16] Mark: Pen tests — frequency and are results shared at high level?
[05:22] Priya: We run annual third-party penetration testing and periodic internal tests. We don't share raw findings but we provide summaries and mitigation status; for enterprise customers we can provide a redacted executive summary as part of the due-diligence exchange.
[05:38] Aisha: On ISO 27001 — is the scope co-terminus with SOC 2 or is it broader? Auditors ask for the ISMS boundary.
[05:47] Priya: The ISO 27001 ISMS boundary is documented in the cert artifact and is generally aligned with our production service offering; there are minor differences in wording. We'll attach the cert so you can see the exact scope text.
[05:58] Tom: Controls mapping — does Redwood provide a mapping to common frameworks like NIST CSF, ISO 27001, and HIPAA so we can crosswalk to our internal control set?
[06:07] Priya: Yes — we maintain a controls mapping spreadsheet that maps Redwood's controls to SOC 2 criteria, ISO 27001 Annex A controls, and common HIPAA safeguards. We'll share that and it usually speeds up customer evidence collection.
[06:19] Tom: Perfect. Example evidence: do you provide screenshots of config change logs or just test reports?
[06:26] Priya: For many items we provide attestations and screenshots where appropriate. For sensitive logs we provide guidance on where auditors can view evidence in the trust center or via a live walkthrough. We avoid sharing raw PII in evidence exports.
[06:40] Mark: Regarding data residency again — if we need EU-only, will Hosted EU guarantee that metadata and logs remain in EU?
[06:49] Jordan: Hosted EU is designed to keep data in EU regions, but we will confirm the exact set of services and any control plane interactions that may touch non-EU endpoints. For absolute assurance we recommend Dedicated or Private deployments. We'll call out the precise flows in the mapping doc.
[07:03] Aisha: For your trust center access model, do customers get read-only portal accounts or is it via shareable links?
[07:10] Priya: We grant customer-level read-only accounts, and for legal/procurement we can generate time-limited shareable links for specific docs. Access is logged.
[07:18] Sara: Any certifications around data processing — are you HIPAA-covered or do you sign a BAA?
[07:24] Jordan: We support HIPAA-covered contracts for enterprise customers and can sign a BAA; there are provisioning and technical requirements that we can review in the follow-up.
[07:33] Tom: On incident response — what's your SLA to notify customers of data incidents and do you provide forensic artifacts?
[07:41] Priya: Our incident response policy mandates notification within 72 hours of confirmation for incidents impacting customer data confidentiality. We provide timelines, root cause, and remediation steps. For customers under a Dedicated contract we offer faster notification SLAs via the support path.
[07:56] Mark: Do you have a vulnerability disclosure program and a public bug bounty?
[08:01] Priya: Yes, we have a VDP and we run a managed bug bounty program with scope listed in the trust center.
[08:09] Luis: Quick question from procurement: pricing for the enterprise tier that includes CMK and longer log retention — high-level ballpark?
[08:16] Jordan: We can send a pricing sheet — enterprise add-ons include CMK support, extended audit retention, and trust center access tiers. I'll attach pricing in the follow-up.
[08:26] Aisha: For the controls mapping spreadsheet, will you map each control to specific artifacts we can drop into our evidence locker?
[08:34] Priya: Yes, we annotate controls with available evidence types (attestation, screenshot, config export, logs) and typical expected auditor questions.
[08:44] Tom: A couple of tricky items: model output retention for PHI-adjacent content, and model training data — do you persist customer prompts for model training?
[08:55] Priya: We do not use customer prompts to train public models; for hosted customers we maintain a separation and we have contractual language for no-training unless opted into. Prompt/response retention and use is configurable by contract. We'll surface the exact clause in the SOC/contract docs.
[09:10] Mark: Good. Can you provide the list of control owners or at least contacts for evidence collection?
[09:17] Priya: We typically assign an evidence coordinator per request and provide a primary contact for audit requests. For Bluecrest we'll have Luis and I support that.
[09:26] Tom: Sounds good. Any red flags from your side about our requirements?
[09:31] Jordan: Nothing immediate — seems like standard enterprise concerns. The main decision points are residency and CMK preference; if you need EU-only and CMK for all flows, Dedicated/Private will be the recommended path.
[09:45] Aisha: One more — do you do quarterly SOC review calls or only on request?
[09:52] Luis: We offer periodic check-ins and can set a cadence that matches your audit cycle.
[09:57] Mark: Okay let's talk next steps.
[10:00] Jordan: Next steps recap: we'll share SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 cert, controls mapping, KMS docs, and a trust center invite. We'll schedule a technical deep-dive with Bluecrest infra folks to map data flows and residency specifics.
[10:15] Tom: That's great. A few clarifying Qs for the follow-up doc: please include exact retention windows for logs, list of subprocessors with locations, and a sample redacted pentest summary.
[10:26] Priya: Noted. We'll include those items.
[10:30] Sara: Procurement needs standard flow-down clause language for BAAs and DPAs — can you include samples?
[10:36] Jordan: Yes, we'll include contract language samples.
[10:40] Aisha: For the deep-dive, we want someone from the infra team who understands the runtime and KV cache behavior.
[10:47] Priya: I'll be on that call and we'll bring one of our runtime engineers to explain caching, KV semantics, and quantization/quant artifacts that might be persisted.
[10:58] Tom: Any questions left from Redwood side?
[11:02] Luis: None.
[11:04] Jordan: Okay we'll follow up with the artifacts. Thanks everyone.
[11:08] Tom: Thanks, appreciate it.

End of transcript.
